Plot an annotated phylogenetic tree

Source: R/mp_tree.R
mp_tree.Rd

Renders the phylogenetic tree stored in a phyloseq::phyloseq object using ggtree, with optional tip colouring by taxonomy and abundance rings drawn with ggtreeExtra. To keep large trees legible, agglomerate with tax.level and/or restrict to the most abundant tips with top.n.

Usage

mp_tree(
  object,
  layout = c("rectangular", "circular", "fan", "radial"),
  annotate = c("abundance", "taxonomy"),
  color.by = NULL,
  group.by = NULL,
  tax.level = NULL,
  top.n = NULL,
  tip.label = FALSE,
  tip.label.size = 2,
  highlight.clades = NULL,
  open.angle = 0,
  palette = NULL,
  theme = NULL,
  plot.title = NULL,
  plot.subtitle = NULL,
  plot.caption = NULL,
  font.size = getOption("micropubr.font.size", 11),
  interactive = FALSE,
  verbose = getOption("micropubr.verbose", FALSE)
)

Arguments

object

A phyloseq::phyloseq object containing a phy_tree.

layout

Tree layout: "rectangular", "circular", "fan" or "radial".

annotate

Annotation layers to draw: any of "abundance" and "taxonomy".

color.by

Taxonomic rank used to colour tip points (e.g. "Phylum").

group.by

Metadata column; when set, the abundance ring becomes a per-group heatmap instead of a single bar.

tax.level

Optional rank to agglomerate to before plotting.

top.n

Optional number of most-abundant tips to retain.

tip.label

Show tip labels.

tip.label.size

Tip-label font size.

highlight.clades

Named list mapping a taxonomic rank to one or more values whose clades should be highlighted, e.g. list(Phylum = "Firmicutes").

open.angle

Opening angle (degrees) for circular/fan layouts.

palette

Palette name or colour vector.

theme

A ggtree theme; defaults to ggtree::theme_tree().

plot.title, plot.subtitle, plot.caption

Optional labels.

font.size

Base font size.

interactive

If TRUE, attempt to return an interactive plotly widget (requires plotly). Experimental for trees: ggtree layers often do not translate, in which case the static plot is returned with a warning. See mp_alpha().

verbose

Print the steps used.

Value

A ggtree/ggplot object, or a plotly widget when interactive = TRUE and the conversion succeeds.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data(GlobalPatterns, package = "phyloseq")
gp <- phyloseq::tax_glom(GlobalPatterns, "Phylum")
mp_tree(gp, layout = "circular", color.by = "Phylum",
        group.by = "SampleType")
} # }
